statusText: The CME weekend halt continues to govern this assessment: nothing has quoted NQ since Friday's 21:00 UTC weekly close and nothing will until roughly 22:00 UTC on Sunday 16 August, about ten hours past the end of this 24-hour horizon. Tail therefore holds at 10% (low), the action stays EA_ON and the status stays green - a pathological one-way price path cannot form while no venue is quoting, and the low non-zero level prices weekend headline discontinuity rather than observed extension. This hour brought continuation rather than new escalation. Lebanon's President Joseph Aoun called the Israeli strikes a "clear message" about the negotiations near 10:37 UTC after a strike on Deir al-Zahrani killed two and wounded nine; the UAE's presidential adviser Anwar Gargash pledged to "safeguard our rights to freedom of navigation" following the third ADNOC tanker attack in a week; and Bloomberg and Al Jazeera both confirm that Iran and Oman still have not reached the accord that would reopen the waterway, with one analyst quoted saying confidence in a deal "is clearly eroding". Stress therefore holds at 53% (elevated) rather than firming again: the escalation ledger has not grown this hour, but neither has it cleared, and the promised U.S. economic-isolation package still lands inside the coming week. The counterweight is unchanged and equally observed - VIX closed Friday at 14.25, less than a point above its 52-week low of 13.38, and the Nasdaq-100 closed down only 0.13% and about 2.3% below its 52-week high. Confidence is 61% (solid): NQ, VIX, WTI and Brent, both key Treasury maturities from two independent sources and the seven-day calendar were each re-read directly this hour, and the price evidence is stale by necessity rather than by omission.
recommendation: Action is EA_ON with a green status, derived from current Tail (10%) alone. No venue quotes NQ anywhere in the 24-hour horizon and no scheduled U.S. macro release falls inside it, so there is no basis for a directional or event-driven block in this window; existing-position management, exits and emergency protection remain active as always. The operative checkpoint sits just beyond the horizon at the CME reopen near 22:00 UTC on Sunday 16 August, and the danger window brackets that reopen together with its first 90 minutes of price discovery - a full weekend of accumulated headlines expresses there as an opening gap, not as intraday structure. Gap risk remains genuinely two-way. Pulling one way: a U.S. economic-isolation package explicitly promised for next week, a presidential claim of sovereignty over the strait that Tehran has publicly rejected, Iran-Oman reopening talks confirmed as still unresolved, 62 commercial ships redirected by the blockade, a third ADNOC vessel struck in under a week, WTI at $82.40 after a +5% week and +33% year with an IEA deficit warning attached, U.S. pump prices at roughly $4.08 a gallon against $3.16 a year ago, and a 10Y at 4.70% pressing a 19-month high. Pulling the other: VIX within a point of its 52-week low, an index that closed the week only 0.13% lower after a third consecutive higher week, and a Friday tape that absorbed the escalation with a mid-range settle rather than a liquidation. Treat the reopen as a checkpoint to be scored on observed price path, not as a pre-committed direction. The dated calendar checkpoints begin Monday and culminate in the FOMC minutes on Wednesday; the undated one - the Treasury's Iran package - is deliberately absent from the verified calendar because no exact date has been published.
headline: Second full weekend day of the CME halt: no new escalation this hour but nothing resolved either, so Tail holds at 10% on EA_ON and Stress holds at 53%.
body:
PRICE PATH (observed, stale by necessity). No venue has quoted NQ since the CME weekly close at 21:00 UTC on Friday 14 August, and none will until the Sunday reopen near 22:00 UTC on 16 August. The last live structure, re-verified this hour from the primary quote page, remains benign: September E-mini Nasdaq-100 futures show a last print of 30,141.75, -46.75 points or -0.15% against a previous close of 30,188.50, with the session settling inside a 30,028.50-30,283.00 band roughly 255 points or 0.84% wide and no close pinned to either extreme. NQ sits about 2.7% below its 52-week high of 30,975.50 against a 52-week low of 22,961.50. The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed at 30,046.14, -38.36 points or -0.13%, about 2.3% below its 52-week high, and the week was the third consecutive higher one. A two-way intraday range with a mid-range settle, several percent off the highs, is the opposite of the persistent directional efficiency, shallow pullbacks, repeated extension and pinning near extremes that the Tail definition requires. Directional efficiency here is not merely low - it is unmeasurable, because nothing has traded for more than fifteen hours.

CROSS-ASSET (observed, Friday close, all re-verified this hour). The split in the evidence remains the central fact of this assessment. Equity volatility is calm to the point of complacency: VIX closed at 14.25, -0.38 or -2.60% on the day, inside a 14.18-14.72 range and only 0.87 points above its 52-week low of 13.38 against a 52-week high of 35.30. Rates and energy say the opposite. The 10-year Treasury yield closed Friday at 4.696%, +5.5bp on the day and at the top of a 4.625-4.700% range, pressing the 52-week high of 4.747% set earlier in the week; the 2-year closed at 4.171%, +3.1bp, against a 52-week range of 3.365-4.370%. The curve is therefore steepening on long-end inflation aversion rather than signalling a growth scare. The Federal Reserve's H.15 release independently corroborates the trajectory into Friday with the 2-year at 4.15% and the 10-year at 4.63% on 13 August and effective fed funds steady at 3.63%. WTI settled at $82.40, +1.42% on the day, +5% on the week, +3.52% on the month and +32.95% on the year; Brent at $88.52, +1.67% on the day, +4.20% on the month and +34.43% on the year, with the move attributed to intensified U.S. economic pressure on Iran, the continuing naval blockade, a Houthi strike on a Red Sea refinery and an IEA warning of the widest 2026 global deficit in five years - against which the IEA also cut its demand outlook because prolonged conflict and high prices are eroding consumption. U.S. pump prices are roughly $4.08 a gallon on the AAA average, about 92 cents above a year ago. Friday's equity weakness was concentrated in semiconductors rather than broad.

GEOPOLITICS (observed, and the only thing moving today). The Strait of Hormuz has been effectively closed since fighting began on 28 February, and the Persian Gulf Strait Authority states it "remains blocked and will not be reopened until Iran's conditions are accepted". The escalation ledger accumulated over earlier hours today is unchanged and unresolved: President Trump said he would declare the strait "a territory of the United States" after defeating Iran, and Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi rejected the claim near 10:37 UTC; Treasury Secretary Bessent's plan to apply "measures like have never been seen in the history of economic isolation on a country" is confirmed for next week and paired with a port blockade that Defense Secretary Hegseth says the Navy can sustain "indefinitely"; CENTCOM counts 62 commercial ships redirected as of Friday; and the ADNOC tanker struck Friday evening was the third ADNOC vessel hit in under a week, fifteen cumulatively, with one crew member killed and twenty injured. What this hour added is confirmation rather than escalation. Bloomberg and Al Jazeera both report that Iran and Oman have still not reached the reopening accord that looked close earlier in the week, with Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi conditioning any reopening on sanctions relief and war reparations and one market analyst quoted saying confidence in a deal "is clearly eroding". The UAE's presidential adviser Anwar Gargash pledged to "safeguard our rights to freedom of navigation" while keeping diplomacy open. Lebanon's President Joseph Aoun called the Israeli strikes a "clear message" about the negotiations near 10:37 UTC, after an IDF strike on Deir al-Zahrani killed two and wounded nine and an earlier strike killed an entire family in Ansar. Houthi forces fired six ballistic missiles at the Red Sea port of Mokha near 08:45 UTC, killing a security guard and wounding eight. Iran's central bank governor said Tehran will soon join the BRICS New Development Bank. Nothing market-relevant has crossed the wires in the hour since the previous assessment.

ASSESSMENT. Tail is held at 10% and stays deep in the low band. Every element the definition asks for - persistent directional efficiency, failed retracements, repeated extension, NQ holding near extremes - is either absent in the last observed session or unobservable in a halted market, and the non-zero level exists to price weekend headline discontinuity that must eventually clear through a gap rather than through intraday structure. That maps to EA_ON and green, and the mapping is mechanical from current Tail alone. Stress holds at 53% (elevated) after four consecutive hours of one-point increments. Holding is the honest reading: this hour produced corroboration of things already scored - stalled reopening talks, a defiant UAE, a Lebanese presidential rebuke - rather than a new escalation leg, so the plausible surprise magnitude at the reopen is unchanged. It is not reduced either, because none of the threads cleared and the promised Treasury package still lands inside the coming week. The counter-evidence is equally observed and equally fresh: a VIX within a point of its 52-week low and an index down 0.13% on the week's final session do not describe a market braced for a difficult high-volatility environment, and the contract is explicit that conflicting signals should raise Stress rather than Tail. dominantMode is mixed for exactly that reason. Confidence is 61% (solid): NQ futures, VIX, WTI and Brent, both key Treasury maturities via two independent sources, the seven-day U.S. calendar and the geopolitical wire were each read directly this hour from primary or exchange-quote pages, and the newly added facts are multiply corroborated rather than single-sourced. Three news domains returned 403 or 451 to direct fetches this hour and were replaced with alternatives that resolved, so no dimension went unverified. The ceiling on confidence is the structural absence of a live price path - a limitation no provider can escape this weekend - not a gap in what was gathered.

lookbackSummary: Across the trailing 24 clock-hours Tail never left the low band, running 2-10% throughout, so the action was EA_ON and the status green in every available slot. Tail held 7-9% across Friday's U.S. cash session, where the data landed and produced two-way volatility and rotation rather than directional efficiency, then printed 6% into the 21:00 UTC weekly close. Stress traced a clear event arc: 38-44% across Friday midday and the U.S. cash session, then easing to 34% at the close. The two runs immediately after the close scored the halt itself at Tail 2% and Stress 12%; from 00:00 UTC onward that reading was corrected back to Tail 9% and Stress 45% on the judgement that a shut venue does not neutralise a live Hormuz closure, and 45% then held for six consecutive hours through 05:00 UTC. From 06:00 UTC the weekend escalation sequence lifted the series steadily - Tail to 10% and Stress through 48%, 50%, 51%, 52% and 53% - as the Mokha barrage, the Lebanon strikes, the ADNOC vessel attack and then the U.S. territorial claim landed one after another with no tape to absorb them. Confidence ran 30-61%, weakest in Friday's pre-data European hours and settling at 59-61% across the weekend halt as each dimension was re-verified hour by hour. The 20:00 UTC slot on 14 August is unavailable because no successful Claude snapshot was published for that hour; those fields are null and no past opinion has been rewritten.
outlookSummary: The entire 24-hour horizon falls inside the CME weekend halt - it runs from 12:00 UTC on Saturday 15 August to 11:00 UTC on Sunday 16 August, ending roughly eleven hours before the reopen near 22:00 UTC that day - so neither a scheduled U.S. macro release nor a tradable price path falls within it. Tail is projected flat at 10% through the Saturday slots, ticking to 11% from 20:00 UTC as the reopen edges into view and to 12% across the Sunday slots; those increments reflect accumulating gap risk, not observed structure, and every slot stays deep in the low band, so the action is EA_ON and the status green throughout. Stress is projected to ease a single point to 52% from 14:00 UTC across the thin Saturday U.S. hours when weekend headline flow is historically lightest, firm back to 53% from 20:00 UTC and then to 54-55% across Sunday as the unresolved threads converge on the reopen. Confidence drifts from 61% to 56% across the horizon as the last live prints age further without replacement. The material catalyst sits just beyond the horizon: the CME reopen and its first 90 minutes of price discovery, which the danger window brackets. Inside the horizon the realistic risks are headline-driven - a further Hormuz vessel strike, an Iranian response to the U.S. territorial claim, an early leak of the promised economic-isolation package, or a breakthrough in the stalled Iran-Oman reopening talks - each of which would move Stress and the expected gap rather than produce observable one-way structure. The first scheduled checkpoint is Monday's Empire State print at 12:30 UTC; the week's highest-impact dated item is the FOMC minutes at 18:00 UTC on Wednesday 19 August, followed by Friday's S&P Global flash PMIs. Its highest-impact undated item is the Treasury's Iran package, omitted from the calendar because no exact date has been published. Nvidia's results on 26 August and the Jackson Hole symposium on 27-29 August both fall outside this seven-day window.

Stress holds at 53%: this hour added continuation rather than escalation - Lebanon's President Aoun called the Israeli strikes a "clear message" near 10:37 UTC, and Bloomberg and Al Jazeera confirm the Iran-Oman reopening accord still has not been reached - none of which changes the split between a VIX at 14.25 and a 10Y at 4.70%.

European Saturday afternoon. No venue, no data, no scheduled catalyst. Tail 10% and Stress 53% simply carry; the realistic mover is a further Hormuz vessel strike or an Iranian response to the U.S. territorial claim, which would lift Stress and the expected reopen gap without producing structure to score.

Weekend headline flow historically thins as the U.S. wakes on a Saturday. Stress eases a single point to 52% to reflect that lull, not a de-escalation; Tail is unchanged at 10% because nothing about the halted tape has changed.
The quietest stretch of the horizon. Tail 10%, Stress 52%, and confidence begins its slow drift as Friday's last live prints age past a full day without replacement.

Still no tape. The blockade, the promised Treasury economic-isolation package and the 62 redirected ships remain unresolved and unpriced; they accumulate into the Sunday gap rather than into any measurable directional efficiency.

Late Saturday afternoon U.S. time. Tail holds at 10% and Stress at 52%. The next genuine checkpoint is still roughly 30 hours away at the CME reopen near 22:00 UTC on Sunday, which the danger window brackets.
